packet.headline_seed: OpenClaw is finally available on Android and iOS
packet.description_seed: The free open source agentic program is finally invading your phone.

what: OpenClaw is finally available on Android and iOS

clean_source_blocks.text: OpenClaw has released standalone apps for both iOS and Android, bringing its agentic AI assistant directly to the App Store and Google Play Store. The launch means users can now interact with OpenClaw’s AI on their smartphones without relying on third‑party chat platforms. From the mobile apps, users can chat with the assistant and choose to grant it access to several parts of the device, including the camera, screen, location, photos, contacts, calendar and reminders. That deeper integration is what makes OpenClaw part of the emerging category of “agentic AI,” where assistants can go beyond text responses and potentially act on information from the device and its sensors. 📱 Native mobile apps, finally💬 Agents in your pocket🔔 Channels, tasks, replies on the go Run agents from wher...

What makes OpenClaw stand out is that it is open source, which means you can inspect how it works or even customize parts of it yourself. That makes it very different from closed AI apps like ChatGPT or Gemini, where most of the backend remains hidden. The iOS version needs iOS 18 or later and is completely free, whereas the Android version requires Android 12 or higher. Early reviews suggest the two apps aren’t quite polished at the same level. The Android app’s interface has been described as rough around the edges, whereas the iOS app looks noticeably more refined and lists itself as a Productivity app that collects no user data according to its App Store listing.

OpenClaw, the open-source AI agent that runs entirely on your own computer, just landed native apps for Android and iOS. The app does not run the AI itself. Instead, it connects to a private gateway you set up yourself on a Mac, PC, or Linux machine, turning your phone into a secure remote for everything that gateway can do. OpenClaw is now on iOS + Android 🦞📱 Native mobile apps, finally💬 Agents in your pocket🔔 Channels, tasks, replies on the goRun agents from wherever your thumbs are.iOS: https://t.co/7LHHc9htgMAndroid: https://t.co/X0Wuh2uA8w

AI agents are the latest “next big thing” for AI, but OpenClaw has been working at the idea for a while now. Today, OpenClaw is bringing a gateway app to Android (and iOS) to help bring agents on the go. It also looks… like that. Announced on Twitter/X, OpenClaw for Android and iOS is designed to let you access agents on the go, paired to the private gateway you may have already set up on other platforms. You can chat with the assistant, including real-time talk, approve actions from your phone, and more. OpenClaw explains what the app can do in the Play Store listing: Pair this Android app with your OpenClaw Gateway to use your phone as a secure node for chat, voice, approvals, and device-aware automation. For OpenClaw users, it’s sure to be a very useful tool. ---

original_article.research:
[Lähde: Android Authority]
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

After months of anticipation, OpenClaw has officially launched its Android and iOS apps, giving users a native way to interact with the AI assistant from their phones. Unfortunately, the debut hasn’t exactly gone according to plan, and many early users are criticizing everything from the app’s interface to its setup process.

If you haven’t heard of OpenClaw before, it’s an open-source AI assistant that runs on your local machine or a cloud server. Rather than connecting to a hosted chatbot, the Android app pairs with your own OpenClaw Gateway, allowing your phone to act as a companion for your AI assistant.

According to the Play Store listing, the app lets you pair with your private OpenClaw Gateway using either a QR code or a setup code. Once connected, you can chat with your assistant from your phone, use a real-time Talk mode with push-to-talk support, review and approve actions requested by your Gateway, and receive push notifications and status updates for connected workflows.

The app can also access your Android phone’s features, such as the camera, screen, location, and notifications, if you choose to grant those permissions. OpenClaw says it’s “local-first,” meaning users remain in control of their Gateway, encryption keys, configuration, and permissions, while device access is managed through Android’s standard permission system.

Getting started with the OpenClaw app is fairly straightforward. You have to set up your OpenClaw Gateway, pair the Android app with it, and then begin using chat, Talk mode, approvals, and automations from your phone.

However, despite the promising feature list, the initial reaction from the OpenClaw community hasn’t been very positive.

Several users commenting on OpenClaw’s X post announcing the new app have complained that the interface feels unfinished. Others said they couldn’t pair the app with their Gateway at all, while some who did manage to connect reported that “nothing works.” Several users appreciated the idea of the app, but said the execution is poor and both the Android and iOS versions feel very raw.

Of course, launch-day hiccups aren’t unusual for such projects, but OpenClaw developers clearly need to look into bug reports and user feedback before pushing the app’s features.

Thank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

---

[Lähde: Digital Trends]
OpenClaw, the open-source AI agent that runs entirely on your own computer, just landed native apps for Android and iOS. The app does not run the AI itself. Instead, it connects to a private gateway you set up yourself on a Mac, PC, or Linux machine, turning your phone into a secure remote for everything that gateway can do.

OpenClaw is now on iOS + Android 🦞📱 Native mobile apps, finally💬 Agents in your pocket🔔 Channels, tasks, replies on the goRun agents from wherever your thumbs are.iOS: https://t.co/7LHHc9htgMAndroid: https://t.co/X0Wuh2uA8w

You can pair your phone to the gateway using a QR code or setup code, a process that takes just a few minutes. Once connected, you can chat with OpenClaw directly or switch to Talk mode for real-time voice conversations. Every action the agent wants to take on your gateway requires your approval first.

You can also share text, links, and media straight from your phone into OpenClaw, and selectively enable device features such as your camera, screen, location, photos, contacts, calendar, and reminders. Push notifications keep you updated on workflow status even when the app sits in the background.

What makes OpenClaw stand out is that it is open source, which means you can inspect how it works or even customize parts of it yourself. That makes it very different from closed AI apps like ChatGPT or Gemini, where most of the backend remains hidden.

The iOS version needs iOS 18 or later and is completely free, whereas the Android version requires Android 12 or higher. Early reviews suggest the two apps aren’t quite polished at the same level.

The Android app’s interface has been described as rough around the edges, whereas the iOS app looks noticeably more refined and lists itself as a Productivity app that collects no user data according to its App Store listing.

OpenClaw’s growing popularity hasn’t gone unnoticed in the industry, and Google is reportedly building its own 24/7 personal agent to compete with it directly.

Pair this Android app with your OpenClaw Gateway to use your phone as a secure node for chat, voice, approvals, and device-aware automation.

For OpenClaw users, it’s sure to be a very useful tool.

payload.title: OpenClaw toi tekoälyagenttinsa Androidille ja iOS:lle
payload.summary: Avoimen lähdekoodin OpenClaw on julkaissut erilliset mobiilisovellukset Androidille ja iOS:lle. Sovellukset toimivat puhelimessa etäkäyttönä käyttäjän omaan OpenClaw Gateway -yhdyskäytävään, eivätkä ne suorita tekoälyä suoraan laitteessa.
payload.content:
OpenClaw on julkaissut omat sovelluksensa Androidille ja iOS:lle, mikä tuo avoimen lähdekoodin tekoälyagentin puhelimiin ilman tarvetta käyttää kolmansien osapuolten keskustelualustoja. Sovellusten kautta käyttäjä voi keskustella avustajan kanssa, hyväksyä toimintoja ja käyttää puhelinta osana itse hallittua OpenClaw Gateway -kokonaisuutta.

## Puhelin toimii yhdyskäytävän etäkäyttönä

OpenClaw ei lähdetietojen mukaan aja tekoälyä suoraan puhelimessa. Sen sijaan mobiilisovellus yhdistetään käyttäjän itse määrittämään yksityiseen Gateway-yhdyskäytävään, joka voi toimia Macilla, Windows-tietokoneella tai Linux-koneella. Käytännössä puhelimesta tulee etäkäyttöväline niihin toimintoihin, joita käyttäjän oma OpenClaw-asennus pystyy tekemään.

Android-sovelluksen kuvauksen mukaan puhelinta voidaan käyttää turvallisena solmuna keskusteluun, puheeseen, hyväksyntöihin ja laitetietoiseen automaatioon. Sovelluksella voi myös käydä reaaliaikaista puhekeskustelua avustajan kanssa sekä hyväksyä toimintoja liikkeellä ollessa.

OpenClaw sijoittuu niin sanottujen tekoälyagenttien joukkoon. Niissä avustaja ei ainoastaan vastaa tekstiin, vaan voi käyttäjän luvalla hyödyntää laitteen tietoja ja toimia niiden perusteella. Mobiilisovelluksissa käyttäjä voi valita, antaako sovellukselle pääsyn esimerkiksi kameraan, näyttöön, sijaintiin, kuviin, yhteystietoihin, kalenteriin ja muistutuksiin.

## Avoin lähdekoodi erottaa palvelun suljetuista kilpailijoista

OpenClawin keskeinen ero moniin tunnettuihin tekoälysovelluksiin on avoin lähdekoodi. Sen toimintaa voi tarkastella ja osia voi muokata itse, kun taas monien suljettujen palvelujen taustajärjestelmät jäävät käyttäjälle näkymättömiksi.

iOS-versio vaatii iOS 18:n tai uudemman käyttöjärjestelmän, ja Android-versio edellyttää Android 12:ta tai uudempaa. Sovellus on saatavilla Applen App Storessa ja Google Play Storessa. iOS-sovellus on lähdetietojen mukaan ilmainen ja se on listattu tuottavuussovellukseksi.

Ensihavaintojen perusteella sovellusten viimeistelyssä on eroja. Android-version käyttöliittymää on kuvattu vielä viimeistelemättömäksi, kun taas iOS-versio vaikuttaa hiotummalta. App Storen listauksen mukaan iOS-sovellus ei kerää käyttäjädataa.
summary_bullets: OpenClaw on julkaissut erilliset sovellukset Androidille ja iOS:lle.
Sovellukset yhdistetään käyttäjän omaan OpenClaw Gateway -yhdyskäytävään, eivätkä ne aja tekoälyä suoraan puhelimessa.
Puhelimella voi keskustella avustajan kanssa, käyttää puhetta ja hyväksyä toimintoja.
iOS-versio vaatii iOS 18:n ja Android-versio Android 12:n tai uudemman.
